newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - February ends on sour note, BFI fall.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - February ends on sour note, BFI fall.

text.p: February and the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) settlement period have ended on a sour note for Paamax owners, brokers said.
The BFI fell 11 points to 1,443 reflecting weaker conditions in the north Atlantic and Pacific, while the caper market remained dull and smaller geared bulkers found poor demand.

In contrast, handymaxes are enjoying firmer rates, especially for short period business in the Far East. Owners report continuing severe weather conditions in the north Atlantic has influenced a number of ballasting vessels to head for Brazil and Argentina instead of the USGulf.

GRAIN - Panamax voyage rates have fallen again in key trades. Korea Line was reported to have fixed the Continental grain-relet Tai Zhou Hai for a mid-March stem of 54,000 tonnes heavy grain USGulf/Japan at $24.25 no combo, down another $0.50 on last done and $1.25 on the rate obtainable last week.

This decline was reflect on a timecharter basis with Bulfracht's fixture of the Frapaco-relet Bunga Srigading 65,921 dwt delivery USGulf mid-March trip Japan at $12,500 daily plus $275,000 ballast bonus.
At the end of last week Atlantic Sovereign 68,641 dwt was fixed for similar business at $2,000 daily higher.

Contrary to some recent expectations, rate levels have not yet improved from east coast south America for panamaxes. Charterers/brokers believe that Brazil/Continent was still fixable at an unchanged $16.50.

Some south American business has been covered on private terms. Oldendorff, was believed to have fixed 50/60,000 tonnes Plate/Malaysia, and the 1975-built Star of Maria 55,012 dwt open spot Ghent may have been booked for an east coast south America round at about $8,000 daily. Docenave was thought to be working a panamax closely delivery north Brazil for two or three laden legs at close to $10,500 daily plus $200,000 ballast bonus.
In the Pacific, Continental was understood to have booked tonnage for 54,000 heavy grain Nopac/Taiwan for March 10/20 at under $14.00. The last reported fixture was at $15.25 by MSK for April 1/10.

MINERALS - Caper business was again limited. Hellas 139,000 dwt was booked on a timecharter basis delivery Continent end March for a trip via Brazil to China at $13,300 daily, not on a voyage basis from Tubarao at $9.50 as reported by some brokers.
Coe and Clerici was believed to be on subjects with Boris Butoma for 100,000 iron ore Port Cartier/Dunkirk west and east for March 15/30 but the rate was kept private.
In the panamax sector, British Steel fixed 60,000/10 iron ore Ponta da Madeira/Immingham for mid March, and NYK covered 35,000 coal Maracaibo/Avonmouth, both on private terms.
Antonis I Angelicoussis 73,000 dwt open prompt Japan was working business closely but again details were not available.
HANDY-SIZES - Handymax demand has strengthened in the Pacific, especially for short period timecharters.
Halla have been linked with Pacific Royal 43,000 dwt delivery Japan mid March for three to five months at $9,400 daily and Pan Ocean are said to have booked tonnage on a similar basis.

Dreyfus was said to have offered a 43,000 dwt vessel in the Far East $10,000 daily for four to six months, and the grab-fitted Unitramp-relet Parisian Trader 43,706 dwt went to MOSK with prompt Far East delivery for two laden legs Pacific trading at a firm $10,200 daily.
E.D.F. Man was thought to have covered at least two vessels of 30/35,000 dwt in the Atlantic but full details were not disclosed.
